outcome.primary_intent: Extract from the official Kubernetes Deployment documentation the documented meaning and the documented default value for three specific fields: .spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable, .spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge, and .spec.progressDeadlineSeconds. The user would not be flexible on missing or incorrect defaults/meanings, and explicitly required preserving any shown percentage rounding behavior and units; they would be flexible on minor paraphrasing/formatting as long as the semantics and documented defaults/behaviors are correctly conveyed.

0.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot is of the Kubernetes “Deployment” documentation page. Near the top of the visible content (just above the “Max Surge” heading), there is text that corresponds to the “Max Unavailable” description. Visible sentences include: “The absolute number is calculated from percentage by rounding down.”, “The value cannot be 0 if .spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge is 0. The default value is 25%.” and an example paragraph starting “For example, when this value is set to 30%, the old ReplicaSet can be scaled down to 70% of desired Pods… ensuring that the total number of Pods available at all times during the update is at least 70% of the desired Pods.” The screenshot does not show the heading label “Max Unavailable” itself, but it shows the associated description text including default and rounding behavior.

The agent’s predicted output states meaning “maximum number of Pods that can be unavailable during an update” and default “25%”. This aligns with what is visible, though the agent output omits the rounding-down behavior that is explicitly visible in the screenshot; per the criterion, rounding behavior should be preserved when present. So this is mostly correct but incomplete on rounding details.
0.discrepancies: Agent predicted output includes meaning and default but does not mention the visible rounding rule (“calculated from percentage by rounding down”) for maxUnavailable. Otherwise, the default value of 25% matches the screenshot text.

1.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot clearly shows the “Max Surge” section heading. The first paragraph includes: “.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge is an optional field that specifies the maximum number of Pods that can be created over the desired number of Pods.” It continues: “The value can be an absolute number (for example, 5) or a percentage of desired Pods (for example, 10%). The value cannot be 0 if maxUnavailable is 0. The absolute number is calculated from the percentage by rounding up. The default value is 25%.”
1.criterion_analysis: The screenshot fully supports the meaning and default value for .spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge, including rounding behavior (percentage rounded up). The agent’s predicted output correctly states the meaning and default (25%), but it does not include the rounding-up behavior that is explicitly shown and required to be preserved when present. This merits partial credit: correct core meaning and default, missing rounding detail.
1.discrepancies: Agent output omits the visible rounding rule (“calculated… by rounding up”) and the constraint about not being 0 if maxUnavailable is 0, both of which appear in the screenshot. The default value (25%) and basic meaning match the screenshot.

2.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Kubernetes documentation page with the in-page heading “Progress Deadline Seconds”. Under it, the visible text reads: “.spec.progressDeadlineSeconds is an optional field that specifies the number of seconds you want to wait for your Deployment to progress before the system reports back that the Deployment has failed progressing - surfaced as a condition with type: Progressing, status: "False" , and reason: ProgressDeadlineExceeded in the status of the resource. The Deployment controller will keep retrying the Deployment. This defaults to 600.” Below that, another visible line says: “If specified, this field needs to be greater than .spec.minReadySeconds.” The page also shows the next section heading “Min Ready Seconds” and part of its description, plus a “Terminating Pods” section header and a blue “Feature State: Beta since Kubernetes v1.35; enabled by default” callout; these are not directly about progressDeadlineSeconds meaning/default beyond confirming the surrounding context. On the right-side table of contents, the link “Progress Deadline Seconds” is highlighted/underlined, indicating the page is positioned at that section.
2.criterion_analysis: The criterion is to report the meaning and default value of .spec.progressDeadlineSeconds from the Deployment documentation. The screenshot directly provides both the meaning (wait time in seconds for deployment to progress before reporting failed progressing; condition type Progressing with status "False" and reason ProgressDeadlineExceeded; controller keeps retrying) and the default (“This defaults to 600.”). This visually supports the agent’s predicted output for this field, including the unit (seconds) and the described failure condition behavior.
2.discrepancies: No contradiction is visible. The screenshot explicitly states the default is 600 and describes the failure-progress condition details that match the agent’s predicted output. The screenshot does not show the agent’s claims about maxUnavailable/maxSurge (those are separate fields), but that is outside this specific criterion.
